input: A gravity settler is employed in order to remove activated sludge from a process stream, and the sizing of the unit is carried out on the basis of the overflow rate. The design overflow rate is 0.8 m h-1 at a throughput of 283 m3 h-1, giving a plan area of 354 m2, a figure that is derived by dividing the throughput by the overflow rate. The overflow rate may be understood as the upward velocity of the clarified stream over the plan of the settler, and it follows that solids which settle more rapidly than this rate are retained within the unit, whilst solids that settle more slowly than it are carried out with the clarified stream. The plan area is therefore the quantity that is fixed jointly by the throughput that has to be handled and the rate at which the stream is permitted to rise, and any increase in the throughput, if the rate is to be maintained, has to be matched by a corresponding increase in the area provided. It should nevertheless be appreciated that the overflow-rate basis on which the sizing rests is a vendor rule that is offered for this particular solid, and that no settling test has in fact been run on the actual slurry that the unit will receive. The area that has been derived is consequently no better than the rule from which it proceeds, and the behaviour of the real slurry, whose settling characteristics may differ in either direction from those that the vendor's rule assumes, remains untested at this stage.
target: A gravity settler removes activated sludge from a process stream. The design overflow rate is 0.8 m h-1 at a throughput of 283 m3 h-1, giving a plan area of 354 m2, derived as the throughput divided by the overflow rate. The overflow rate is the upward velocity of the clarified stream over the settler plan. Solids that settle faster than the overflow rate are retained; solids that settle more slowly leave with the clarified stream. The plan area is the quantity the throughput and the rate fix between them: at a stated rate, a larger throughput requires a larger area in the same proportion, and the area states the size at which the rising stream moves at the design rate. The sizing rests on the overflow rate, and the overflow rate rests on a vendor rule. The overflow-rate basis is a vendor rule for this solid, and no settling test on the actual slurry has been run. The rule gives the area a stated basis, but the basis is the vendor's experience of the solid, not a measurement of the slurry the settler will receive. Sludge settling varies with the state of the sludge, and a slurry that settles more slowly than the rule assumes leaves the settler loaded with solids the design did not intend to pass. The derived area is therefore the size the rule requires, held at the rule's accuracy: it is the area to build if the vendor basis is accepted, and the settling test that would replace the rule with a measurement has not been run.
